# Proposal output

When a runner returns proposals, the gate reports them three ways on the PR: the `pollux-agent` check run (`action_required`, listing doc paths and reasons), one review comment per proposal on the head commit, and one summary comment on the PR. A "no impact" result sets the check to `success` with the reason and posts no comments. Proposals are acted on from those comments (see [Acting on proposals](#acting-on-proposals)).

## Failures and Re-run

Every analysis first creates an in-progress check and saves an armed run (nonce, 10-minute deadline), so a check is never missing or left pending: the deadline sweep closes any armed run neutral (see [Job queue](job-queue.md)). Any failure ends the check neutral, titled "Analysis failed" (or "PR too large to analyze"), with a one-line fixed cause that never quotes model output, provider responses, or artifact text; the detail stays in the server log. A superseded or interrupted analysis is not a failure: the next analysis closes its check as superseded.

A successful summary opens with "**pollux-agent** proposes N doc update(s)." (open proposals only) and has no Re-run box. After a failure the summary instead opens with the cause and ends with an unticked "- [ ] Re-run analysis". Proposals from an earlier successful run stay listed and are not marked outdated, because a failure says nothing about them. Ticking the box (an edited `issue_comment` on the bot's summary comment, identified by its saved comment ID; a tick on any other comment or any other edit does nothing) or clicking GitHub's Re-run on the check (`check_run` `rerequested`) enqueues a `pull_request`-kind job. The tick goes through the same sender check as every other comment action: the sender needs write access, otherwise the bot replies, reacts 😕 and unticks the box. Clicking Re-run on the check needs no check of its own, because GitHub only lets people with write access do it. The job fetches the PR's current head and starts a fresh analysis with a new check run, and the box is unticked when that analysis next writes the summary (on its result or its failure; an Actions re-run leaves it ticked until the workflow finishes). A re-run of a closed PR, or a second one while an analysis of the same head is still running, does nothing, so repeated ticks cannot stack model runs.

A re-run waits for an analysis already running on the PR instead of cancelling it, and a push supersedes a re-run like any analysis, so only the newest head produces the final check; a same-head check it replaces reads "Superseded by a re-run". For forks, `check_run` may carry no pull request; the handler then finds the PR by the check's head SHA in stored state. Posting comments after a result is retried a few times with backoff, and a retry adopts comments already created by their markers, so nothing is duplicated.

## Acting on proposals

The summary and the proposal comments carry the controls. Every action needs the sender to have write access to the repo (checked through the GitHub API); without it the bot replies, reacts 😕, and unticks the box. Bot senders are ignored. An accepted action gets 👀 while it runs, replaced by 🚀 when done or 😕 when refused with a reply saying why. A comment that asks for nothing costs no GitHub call.

- **Apply this change** (checkbox on a checkbox-variant proposal comment): applies that proposal.
- **Apply all** (summary checkbox) or `/pollux-agent apply`: applies every open proposal.
- **Skip this commit** / **Skip this PR** (summary checkboxes) or `/pollux-agent skip <reason>` / `/pollux-agent skip-pr <reason>`: concludes the check `success` titled "Skipped by @user". A tick or a command without a reason makes the bot ask for one, and the asker's next comment on the PR becomes the reason. The reason is flattened to one line, capped at 500 characters, and has `@` mentions and checkbox markup broken so it notifies nobody. A commit skip covers only the head it was made on; a PR skip covers every later push, and its proposals are no longer refreshed.

Commands are read only from the first line of a PR conversation comment; a review comment starting with the prefix does nothing. Ticks are detected from the edit itself: exactly one `- [ ]` line went to `- [x]`, so other edits to the bot's comments do nothing.

Apply splices each proposal's content over the original section text it stored, in the doc read at the head SHA, and makes one commit on the PR branch (`docs: apply pollux-agent proposal for …`, or `… N pollux-agent proposals`), moving the branch without forcing. A new doc is created and its index entry is added to the `## Index` list of `docs/README.md`. Nothing is committed, and the bot says why, when:

- the PR is from a fork (the bot cannot push to it), or is closed;
- the proposals are stale: the head moved since they were made, a re-analysis is pending, a PR skip is active, or the last analysis failed (tick Re-run first);
- a proposal no longer matches the doc (section text not found exactly once, doc missing, or a new doc that already exists), or a stored proposal's target is invalid;
- the branch moved while committing, or GitHub rejected the commit (protected branch, symlink or submodule at the doc path).

After a commit the proposal is `applied` with the commit's SHA, its Apply box is ticked, the summary is redrawn, and a reply "Applied in <sha>" is posted under its comment. The gate saves a pending apply (proposal IDs, message, parent) before committing. If the process dies after GitHub accepted the commit, the retry or the push webhook of that commit finds it (our bot, that message, that parent, at the tip or one below it) and adopts it instead of committing twice, so the push does not mark the proposals outdated. Redelivering an apply only posts what is still missing, found by hidden markers in the replies.

## Where the section text comes from

Each proposal carries the current text of the section it replaces and that text's head-side line range in the doc. The server runner fills both from its own checkout of the head commit (see [Server runner](server-runner.md)); the Actions runner fills them from the doc fetched at the head SHA through the contents API (see [Actions runner](actions-runner.md)); they are never model output and are kept out of the generated JSON schema. Both are empty for a new doc. The range runs from the heading through the section's last line, including trailing blank lines. The gate may import only `internal/review`, so it cannot parse docs itself; it trusts these fields. A proposal whose doc or section is missing at the head, or whose heading matches more than one section, leaves them empty, and its comment degrades to the checkbox variant; guessing the section would let a suggestion overwrite the wrong one. Without the original text Apply refuses the proposal.

A proposal's content replaces the whole section, heading line included, because a suggestion replaces the heading line too. Both runner prompts and the generated schema say so. If the content still starts without a heading of the section's level, the gate puts back the original heading and the blank lines after it before rendering; otherwise applying the edit would delete the heading from the doc. A proposal's `doc_path` must be under `docs/` and end in `.md` or `.mdx`.

## Two comment variants

- **Suggestion.** Used only when the whole section, trailing blank lines included, lies inside one head-side hunk of that doc in the PR diff. GitHub only accepts review comments on diff lines, so this is the one case where the comment can sit on the doc's own lines. It is a GitHub `suggestion` block replacing exactly those lines, with the reason and no checkbox; GitHub's own Commit suggestion button applies it. The suggestion restates the section's trailing blank lines, otherwise applying it would eat the gap before the next heading. The code fence is made longer than any backtick run in the content so proposed code fences cannot close it early.
- **Checkbox.** Used for everything else: the doc is not in the diff, the section only partly overlaps a hunk or spans two, or the doc is new. The comment sits on the proposal's anchor line (a changed code line) and holds the reason, the doc path and section, the edit as a `diff` block (old section lines `-`, new lines `+`; a new doc shows only added lines plus its index entry), and an unticked "Apply this change" task-list item.

## Identity and re-runs

A proposal's identity is its doc path plus its normalized section heading (leading `#` and whitespace stripped; path alone for a new doc), hashed to a short ID. The gate remembers each proposal's ID, comment ID and URL, and state (`open`, `applied`, or `outdated`), plus the summary comment ID, per PR.

On each run, after the check run is created, the gate reconciles the new proposals against what it remembers:

- **Same proposal again:** its comment is edited in place. The PR's comment count does not change across pushes.
- **New proposal:** a new review comment.
- **Proposal gone:** its comment and summary row are marked `outdated`; the old body stays readable under an "Outdated" notice. The gate never deletes a comment: that would erase the thread's replies and history, and a proposal that returns would have to start over. A proposal that returns after being outdated reopens its old comment.
- **No impact:** every earlier proposal is marked outdated and the check is `success`.
- **Summary:** one issue comment listing every proposal with doc path, section, a link to its comment, and state, plus the Apply all and Skip boxes. It is edited in place, and only created when there is something to list or one already exists.

A comment keeps its location and variant across edits. GitHub cannot move a review comment, and replacing it would churn the thread. A suggestion block on the wrong lines would overwrite them when applied, so on edit the suggestion body is used only if the existing comment already sits on that doc at the same lines; otherwise the body is the checkbox variant. If a user deletes a proposal's comment, an open proposal gets a fresh comment, and an outdated one is skipped rather than resurrected.

## Markers and crash recovery

Every proposal comment starts with a hidden `<!-- pollux-agent:proposal:ID -->` and the summary with `<!-- pollux-agent:summary -->`. The gate lists the PR's comments before writing and, when its stored state lacks a comment ID, adopts the comment carrying the marker. It adopts or edits only comments written by the App's own bot user, with the marker as the body's first line: anyone can paste a marker into a comment (proposal IDs are hashes of public data), and adopting theirs would make every later edit fail with 403. So if a run stops after GitHub accepted a comment but before the gate saved its ID, the next run reuses that comment instead of posting a second. Before its first create, a run saves the proposals it is about to post, so even a run that crashed on its very first post leaves state behind; the next run then lists comments and adopts or outdates them, including when it finds no impact. State is saved again after all writes succeed. The concluded state (check done, run cleared) is saved before comments are posted, so a comment failure cannot leave an armed run for the deadline sweep to overwrite a success with neutral. Any other failed run is redone by the next push or re-run (see [Job queue](job-queue.md)).

## Known limits

- If a later push deletes the anchor line, GitHub shows its own "Outdated" badge on a still-open proposal; the gate's state is unaffected.
- The two GitHub comment APIs (review and issue) have separate ID spaces and edit endpoints, so the gate tracks which kind each comment is.

A later push still supersedes a queued or running re-run, so only the newest head produces the final check.
- **Job kinds.** `pull_request` (supersedes), `comment` (an Apply, Apply all, or Skip request from a comment tick or `/pollux-agent` command; it supersedes nothing and runs in order with the PR's other jobs), `workflow_run` (an Actions analysis run finished), and `run_deadline` (an awaited run passed its deadline). A Re-run tick on the summary is not a `comment` job: it is queued as a `pull_request`-kind re-run so a push can supersede it. A sweep every 30 seconds enqueues one `run_deadline` job per overdue awaited run; its delivery ID is `deadline:<nonce>` plus the current minute, so sweeps within a minute dedupe and a deadline job whose GitHub write was rejected is retried the next minute until the check is closed. - **No job-level retry.** A failed job is recorded with its error and not retried; the next push or re-run for the PR replaces it. ## Flow (phase 1 target)

1. A PR is opened or updated; GitHub sends `pull_request` to the backend.
2. The backend lists the PR's changed files; the analysis runner maps them to docs through each doc's `covers` globs on its own checkout of the head commit (see [0002](decisions/0002-docs-structure.md)).
3. The LLM compares the diff with those docs and returns "no impact" or proposed edits.
4. The backend sets the `pollux-agent` check: `success` for no impact, `action_required` otherwise, and posts one review comment per proposal plus a summary comment (see [Proposal output](features/proposal-output.md)).
4a. If analysis fails or the PR is over the size limits, the check ends neutral with a fixed cause and the summary offers a "Re-run analysis" checkbox; GitHub's Re-run on the check does the same. The check never stays pending.
5. Someone with write access applies one proposal or all of them (a checkbox or `/pollux-agent apply`), which commits to the PR branch, or skips the check for one commit or the whole PR with a reason (a checkbox or `/pollux-agent skip`, `skip-pr`). Comment events arrive as `issue_comment` and `pull_request_review_comment` webhooks and run as `comment` jobs. Applying on a fork PR is refused. The check turns green and the PR can merge.

proposals.content:
# Proposal output

When a runner returns proposals, the gate reports them three ways on the PR: the `pollux-agent` check run (`action_required`, listing doc paths and reasons), one review comment per proposal on the head commit, and one summary comment on the PR. A "no impact" result sets the check to `success` with the reason and posts no comments. The comments are also the controls: Apply, Apply all, Skip, and Re-run are checkboxes or `/pollux-agent` commands (see [Apply and Skip](#apply-and-skip)).

## Failures and Re-run

Every analysis first creates an in-progress check and saves an armed run (nonce, 10-minute deadline), so a check is never missing or left pending: the deadline sweep closes any armed run neutral (see [Job queue](job-queue.md)). Any failure ends the check neutral, titled "Analysis failed" (or "PR too large to analyze"), with a one-line fixed cause that never quotes model output, provider responses, or artifact text; the detail stays in the server log. A superseded or interrupted analysis is not a failure: the next analysis closes its check as superseded.

A successful summary opens with "**pollux-agent** proposes N doc update(s)." (open proposals only) and has no Re-run box. After a failure the summary instead opens with the cause and ends with an unticked "- [ ] Re-run analysis". Proposals from an earlier successful run stay listed and are not marked outdated, because a failure says nothing about them. Ticking the box (an edited `issue_comment` on the PR's saved summary comment, made by a non-bot sender; a tick on any other comment or any other edit does nothing) or clicking GitHub's Re-run on the check (`check_run` `rerequested`) enqueues a `pull_request`-kind job. It fetches the PR's current head and starts a fresh analysis with a new check run, and the box is unticked when that analysis next writes the summary (on its result or its failure; an Actions re-run leaves it ticked until the workflow finishes). A re-run of a closed PR, or a second one while an analysis of the same head is still running, does nothing, so repeated ticks cannot stack model runs. A Re-run tick goes through the same write-access check as the other comment actions.

A re-run waits for an analysis already running on the PR instead of cancelling it, and a push supersedes a re-run like any analysis, so only the newest head produces the final check; a same-head check it replaces reads "Superseded by a re-run". For forks, `check_run` may carry no pull request; the handler then finds the PR by the check's head SHA in stored state. Posting comments after a result is retried a few times with backoff, and a retry adopts comments already created by their markers, so nothing is duplicated.

## Apply and Skip

Comment events (`issue_comment` created or edited, `pull_request_review_comment` edited) from non-bot senders are turned into intents; comments that ask for nothing cost no GitHub call. Actions:

- **Apply** (tick "Apply this change" on a proposal's review comment) and **Apply all** (tick in the summary, or `/pollux-agent apply`). The open proposals targeted are spliced into the docs at the head commit and pushed as one commit to the PR branch, without forcing. A section proposal's stored original text must occur exactly once in the doc; a new-doc proposal fails if the doc already exists; its index entry is added to the end of the `## Index` list in `docs/README.md`.
- **Skip this commit** and **Skip this PR** (ticks in the summary, or `/pollux-agent skip <reason>` and `/pollux-agent skip-pr <reason>`). A skip needs a reason. A tick or a command without one makes the bot ask, and that user's next comment on the PR becomes the reason; a push before then cancels the ask with a note. The reason is cleaned (one line, capped, @mentions and checkbox markup defused) before it is echoed. A skip concludes the check `success` titled "Skipped by @user". A commit skip covers only the head it was made at; a PR skip carries over to every later push, which concludes the check skipped without analysis and stops refreshing proposals.

Every action first requires write access for the sender (a sender without it gets a reply and a refusal reaction). The bot reacts 👀 when it picks the action up, then swaps it for 🚀 when done or 😕 when refused with a reply saying why; a refused tick is unticked again. Commands are read only on issue (conversation) comments.

Apply refuses, with a reply and nothing committed, when: the PR is from a fork (the bot cannot push; the comments say so), the PR is closed, the proposals are not for the live head (a newer push is being re-analyzed, the last analysis failed, or the PR is skipped), a stored proposal fails validation, a proposal no longer matches the doc, the branch moved while applying, or GitHub rejects the commit (protected branch, symlink or submodule at a doc path). A successful apply marks the proposals `applied` with the commit SHA, ticks their boxes for Apply all, redraws the summary, and replies "Applied in <sha>" under each proposal comment.

Crash recovery: the pending apply (proposal IDs, commit message, parent SHA) is saved before the commit. If the commit landed but the state was not saved, the next Apply, or the push event of that commit (or of a user push on top of it), finds the bot's own commit by author, message, and parent, adopts it, and marks the proposals applied instead of outdating them. A redelivered Apply only posts what is still missing; replies are adopted by a hidden `applied:ID:SHA` marker.

## Where the section text comes from

Each proposal carries the current text of the section it replaces and that text's head-side line range in the doc. The server runner fills both from its own checkout of the head commit (see [Server runner](server-runner.md)); the Actions runner fills them from the doc fetched at the head SHA through the contents API (see [Actions runner](actions-runner.md)); they are never model output and are kept out of the generated JSON schema. Both are empty for a new doc. The range runs from the heading through the section's last line, including trailing blank lines. The gate may import only `internal/review`, so it cannot parse docs itself; it trusts these fields. A proposal whose doc or section is missing at the head, or whose heading matches more than one section, leaves them empty, and its comment degrades to the checkbox variant; guessing the section would let a suggestion overwrite the wrong one. Apply splices on the stored original text, so such a proposal cannot be applied.

A proposal's content replaces the whole section, heading line included, because a suggestion replaces the heading line too. Both runner prompts and the generated schema say so. If the content still starts without a heading of the section's level, the gate puts back the original heading and the blank lines after it before rendering; otherwise applying the edit would delete the heading from the doc. A proposal's `doc_path` must end in `.md` or `.mdx`.

## Two comment variants

- **Suggestion.** Used only when the whole section, trailing blank lines included, lies inside one head-side hunk of that doc in the PR diff. GitHub only accepts review comments on diff lines, so this is the one case where the comment can sit on the doc's own lines. It is a GitHub `suggestion` block replacing exactly those lines, with the reason and no checkbox. The suggestion restates the section's trailing blank lines, otherwise applying it would eat the gap before the next heading. The code fence is made longer than any backtick run in the content so proposed code fences cannot close it early.
- **Checkbox.** Used for everything else: the doc is not in the diff, the section only partly overlaps a hunk or spans two, or the doc is new. The comment sits on the proposal's anchor line (a changed code line) and holds the reason, the doc path and section, the edit as a `diff` block (old section lines `-`, new lines `+`; a new doc shows only added lines plus its index entry), and an unticked "Apply this change" task-list item (replaced by a note on a fork PR).

## Identity and re-runs

A proposal's identity is its doc path plus its normalized section heading (leading `#` and whitespace stripped; path alone for a new doc), hashed to a short ID. The gate remembers each proposal's ID, comment ID and URL, and state (`open`, `applied`, or `outdated`), plus the summary comment ID, per PR.

On each run, after the check run is created, the gate reconciles the new proposals against what it remembers:

- **Same proposal again:** its comment is edited in place. The PR's comment count does not change across pushes.
- **New proposal:** a new review comment.
- **Proposal gone:** its comment and summary row are marked `outdated`; the old body stays readable under an "Outdated" notice. The gate never deletes a comment: that would erase the thread's replies and history, and a proposal that returns would have to start over. A proposal that returns after being outdated reopens its old comment.
- **No impact:** every earlier proposal is marked outdated and the check is `success`.
- **Summary:** one issue comment listing every proposal with doc path, section, a link to its comment, and state. It is edited in place, and only created when there is something to list or one already exists.

A comment keeps its location and variant across edits. GitHub cannot move a review comment, and replacing it would churn the thread. A suggestion block on the wrong lines would overwrite them when applied, so on edit the suggestion body is used only if the existing comment already sits on that doc at the same lines; otherwise the body is the checkbox variant. If a user deletes a proposal's comment, an open proposal gets a fresh comment, and an outdated one is skipped rather than resurrected.

## Markers and crash recovery

Every proposal comment starts with a hidden `<!-- pollux-agent:proposal:ID -->` and the summary with `<!-- pollux-agent:summary -->`. The gate lists the PR's comments before writing and, when its stored state lacks a comment ID, adopts the comment carrying the marker. It adopts or edits only comments written by the App's own bot user, with the marker as the body's first line: anyone can paste a marker into a comment (proposal IDs are hashes of public data), and adopting theirs would make every later edit fail with 403. So if a run stops after GitHub accepted a comment but before the gate saved its ID, the next run reuses that comment instead of posting a second. Before its first create, a run saves the proposals it is about to post, so even a run that crashed on its very first post leaves state behind; the next run then lists comments and adopts or outdates them, including when it finds no impact. State is saved again after all writes succeed. The concluded state (check done, run cleared) is saved before comments are posted, so a comment failure cannot leave an armed run for the deadline sweep to overwrite a success with neutral. Any other failed run is redone by the next push or re-run (see [Job queue](job-queue.md)).

## Known limits

- If a later push deletes the anchor line, GitHub shows its own "Outdated" badge on a still-open proposal; the gate's state is unaffected.
- The two GitHub comment APIs (review and issue) have separate ID spaces and edit endpoints, so the gate tracks which kind each comment is.
- Apply is not available on fork PRs.

## Guarantees

- **Deduplicated by delivery.** A repeated `X-GitHub-Delivery` ID is acknowledged and changes nothing, including after a restart.
- **One job per PR at a time.** Jobs share a key (`owner/repo#number`); jobs with the same key run in order, one at a time, and different PRs run in parallel up to a fixed cap.
- **Newer push wins.** A `pull_request` job supersedes older jobs with the same key and kind: pending ones are skipped, a running one has its context cancelled. Jobs of other kinds are not affected. A re-run (see [Proposal output](proposal-output.md)) is a `pull_request`-kind job too but does not supersede: it queues behind a running analysis on the same key, so it never cancels one and then skips. A later push still supersedes a queued or running re-run, so only the newest head produces the final check.
- **Job kinds.** `pull_request` (supersedes), `comment` (a user's Apply, Skip, or skip-reason comment; does not supersede, so it queues behind a running analysis for the PR), `workflow_run` (an Actions analysis run finished), and `run_deadline` (an awaited run passed its deadline). A sweep every 30 seconds enqueues one `run_deadline` job per overdue awaited run; its delivery ID is `deadline:<nonce>` plus the current minute, so sweeps within a minute dedupe and a deadline job whose GitHub write was rejected is retried the next minute until the check is closed. A deadline job for a run that has since completed or been replaced by a new push does nothing.
- **At least once.** A job running at shutdown or crash stays `running` and is requeued on the next start, so it can run twice. Every handler must be safe to repeat for the same payload.
- **No job-level retry.** A failed job is recorded with its error and not retried; the next push or re-run for the PR replaces it. The only retry is the deadline job, which backstops a check left in progress: it is re-enqueued with exponential backoff (about 0, 1, 2, 4, 8 … 1024 minutes past the deadline, then every 4 hours) and given up, with a warning in the log, once the run is a day overdue.

# Deploying pollux

Production is a single host running the backend under Docker Compose. A systemd timer deploys `origin/main` whenever it moves.

## Image and container

- The `Dockerfile` builds the server and the `healthcheck` probe (`backend/cmd/healthcheck`) into a distroless, non-root image. The image has no shell or curl, which is why the health probe is a Go binary.
- `compose.yaml` runs one `pollux` service: read-only root file system, `/tmp` on tmpfs, all capabilities dropped, `no-new-privileges`, and port 8080 published on `127.0.0.1` only. Put a reverse proxy in front for GitHub's webhooks.
- Configuration comes from `.env` next to `compose.yaml`. `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` in `.env` must be the host path of the App's private key; compose is refused without it. It is bind-mounted read-only into the container, and `DATABASE_PATH` and `ADDR` are fixed by compose.
- The SQLite database lives in the `pollux-data` volume at `/data`, so it survives rebuilds.
- The health check passes only when `GET /healthz` returns exactly 200.

## Auto-update

`deploy/pollux-update.timer` starts `deploy/pollux-update.service` one minute after boot and every 2 minutes after that. The service runs `deploy/pollux-update.sh` from the checkout at `~/pollux-agent`.

Each run, under a lock so runs never overlap:

1. Fetches `origin/main`. It does nothing if that commit is already the deployed one or the recorded failed one.
2. Checks out the commit detached and runs `docker compose up -d --build --wait`.
3. On success, records the commit as deployed.
4. On failure, records it as failed so the timer does not retry it, rolls back to the last deployed commit if there is one, and exits non-zero. The next merge to `main` clears the failure.

State is kept in `$XDG_STATE_HOME/pollux` (default `~/.local/state/pollux`): `deployed`, `failed`, and `lock`.

See [Setup](setup.md) for running the backend locally and [Registering the GitHub App](github-app.md) for the App and its key.

## Compose service

- Read-only root file system with a `/tmp` tmpfs, all capabilities dropped, `no-new-privileges`.

Reasons (proposal comments, the check run's proposal list, and a no-impact reason) are rendered as one line capped at 1000 characters, with control, bidi and zero-width-space characters dropped. They cannot mention, link or autolink, embed an image, open HTML, decode an entity, start a block (heading, quote, list, checkbox, rule), or link an issue or PR (`#N`, `GH-N`); balanced inline code spans are kept as written and any other backtick is escaped. Doc paths, sections and index entries are each shown as a single inline code span (in summary table cells too, with `|` escaped). The check run's proposal list stops with "… and N more" before the size limit so a code span is never cut. A failure cause is always a fixed string chosen by the gate, never model or artifact text.

- **Suggestion.** Used only when the whole section, trailing blank lines included, lies inside one head-side hunk of that doc in the PR diff. GitHub only accepts review comments on diff lines, so this is the one case where the comment can sit on the doc's own lines. It is a GitHub `suggestion` block replacing exactly those lines, with the reason and no checkbox. The suggestion restates the section's trailing blank lines, otherwise applying it would eat the gap before the next heading. The code fence is made longer than any backtick run in the content so proposed code fences cannot close it early.
- **Checkbox.** Used for everything else: the doc is not in the diff, the section only partly overlaps a hunk or spans two, or the doc is new. ## Skip

Skip has two scopes: this commit (the check passes for the current head; the next push is analyzed again) and this PR (the check passes for every later push and no analysis runs).

## First deploy

1. Create the GitHub App by following [Registering the GitHub App](github-app.md). Keep the App ID, webhook secret, and downloaded `.pem`.
2. Store the key outside the repo, readable by the container user. The key is normally `0600` owned by you, which uid 65532 cannot read. Make the file world-readable inside a directory only you can enter; Docker mounts it as root, so the directory's mode doesn't stop the container, but it keeps other host users out:

   ```
   install -d -m 700 ~/.config/pollux-agent
   mv <key>.pem ~/.config/pollux-agent/github-app.pem
   chmod 0444 ~/.config/pollux-agent/github-app.pem
   ```

3. Clone the repo to `~/pollux-agent` (`git clone https://github.com/mrkizildag/pollux-agent ~/pollux-agent`); `deploy/pollux-deploy.sh` uses that path unless `POLLUX_DIR` says otherwise. Copy `backend/.env.example` to `.env` at the repo root and fill it in (variables are listed in [Setup](setup.md)). Compose uses `.env` both as the container's `env_file` and for its own interpolation. Set `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE` to the **host** path of the key. Compose bind-mounts it read-only at `/run/secrets/github-app.pem` and overrides the variable inside the container. It also overrides `DATABASE_PATH` and `ADDR`, so those two values in `.env` are ignored under compose.
4. Start it:

   ```
   docker compose up -d --build
   ```

5. Enable Funnel. In the tailnet admin console, allow HTTPS certificates for the tailnet and grant the node the `funnel` node attribute in the policy file. Changing Funnel needs root unless you ran `sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER` once. It replaces whatever Funnel already serves on `/` of port 443. Then on the host:

   ```
   tailscale funnel --bg 8080
   tailscale funnel status
   ```

   `status` prints the public URL. `--bg` keeps the config across reboots. Funnel only serves ports 443, 8443, and 10000 publicly; here it proxies 443 to `localhost:8080`.
6. Set the App's webhook URL to `https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net/webhook`.

### Verify

```
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz
```

prints `ok`. Then in the App's "Advanced → Recent deliveries", redeliver the `ping`; it should return `202`.

## Retention

The worker prunes old rows so the database does not grow forever. The first prune runs a minute after start (so a server restarted more often than hourly still prunes), then every hour. The branch `pollux-agent/docs-scaffold` is created off the default tip, with one commit and one PR into the default branch. The validated files are stored as soon as they are written, so a failed commit or PR step retries without running the model again. A crash after the branch or PR exists is recovered by adopting them, not creating duplicates.

Any failure before the PR exists, including a workflow run that fails, is cancelled, or passes its deadline, leaves the repo's state retryable. Waiting checks then say an attempt failed, and the next PR event on a docs-less PR tries again. After 3 failed attempts the scaffold stops for good and the checks say it could not be written, so `docs/` has to be added by hand.

## Parts

- **Backend** (`backend/`, Go): receives GitHub webhooks, talks to the GitHub and LLM APIs, owns the check run. `POST /webhook` first applies token-bucket rate limits (one global bucket plus one per client IP) and answers 429 with `Retry-After: 1` before reading the body or checking the signature; the client IP is the TCP peer, or the first `X-Forwarded-For` entry only when the peer is loopback (as behind Tailscale Funnel), so direct clients cannot forge it. It then verifies GitHub's signature. For a `pull_request` event (opened, synchronize, reopened), a `workflow_run` completed event for a run the backend dispatched, or a human `issue_comment` or `pull_request_review_comment` event, it stores the delivery and a durable job in one SQLite transaction, deduplicated by GitHub's delivery ID; other events are acknowledged without being stored. A periodic sweep enqueues a deadline job for each awaited Actions run past its deadline, and the worker deletes finished jobs and their deliveries after 7 days (see [Job queue](features/job-queue.md)). Accepted deliveries return 202. A worker processes jobs off that queue: it runs at most one job per key at a time (a PR, or a repo's scaffold) but keys in parallel, a newer push supersedes the older job for the same PR, cancelling it if it is already running, and jobs left unfinished by a restart resume afterward. The `pull_request` job picks an analysis runner for the repo and reports its result as the `pollux-agent` check run on the PR head commit.
- **Frontend** (phase 2, TypeScript + shadcn/ui): org and repo settings, configurable docs structures.
- **Doc targets**: phase 1 writes to the repo's own `docs/` folder. Notion comes in phase 3.

## Webhook URL and secret

GitHub needs a reachable HTTPS URL to deliver events to `POST /webhook`. For local dev, expose the backend with `tailscale funnel 8080` and use the resulting Tailscale Funnel hostname: `https://<host>/webhook`. For production, the URL is `https://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net/webhook` from the Funnel set up in [Deploy](deploy.md).

Generate the webhook secret with `openssl rand -hex 32`. Set the same value in the App's webhook secret field and in `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (see [Setup](setup.md)). The backend rejects any delivery whose `X-Hub-Signature-256` doesn't match this secret.

The endpoint is rate limited before the body is read or the signature is checked, so a throttled request gets `429` with `Retry-After: 1` even if its signature is bad. Limits are token buckets: 80 requests/s (burst 160) across all clients and 30 requests/s (burst 60) per client IP, sized so normal GitHub delivery volume for one installation is not throttled. The client IP is the TCP peer; only when the peer is loopback (as behind Tailscale Funnel) is the first `X-Forwarded-For` entry used, so direct clients cannot forge it. A throttled delivery can be redelivered from "Advanced → Recent deliveries".
